hypothesis: W-R18's 79.2% mean-transition accuracy suggests sparse local changes can be hidden by averaging 15 edges. A maximum local-edge mismatch or top-three local-edge pooled statistic, calibrated only on fresh development inputs, may detect unseen two-swap negatives better. This is a new frozen test; W-R18 heldout never enters calibration.
generator: EXACT frozen W-R18 nonlinear four-channel 16-tick synthetic generator and genuine per-tick offset/jitter; development seeds 56-59 with train reversals and rotate-three negatives; heldout seeds60-63 with a novel TWO adjacent-tail-pair swaps (at positions 5/6 and 10/11). Preserve candidate anchor and unordered observation multiset for both labels.
arms: unordered anchor-relative modulo16 histogram difference, scalar train-only threshold (negative control)
mean 15 adjacent circular transition mismatches, scalar train-only threshold
maximum of 15 adjacent transition mismatches, scalar train-only threshold
mean of three largest local transition mismatches, scalar train-only threshold
training: One scalar threshold per arm, equal 72 training labeled pairs, threshold midpoint of train-only max positive and min negative score, no heldout labels, no post-result tuning or additional model parameters.
primary: Compute per-arm 72 heldout pair accuracy and per-seed confusion. SPARSE_EDGE_TRANSFER if max-edge OR top3 >=0.85, histogram<=0.55, and the winning local statistic strictly beats mean edges; PARTIAL if any max/top3 beats mean edges but below criterion; NEGATIVE otherwise. Preserve other arms and false-positive rates.
validity: Distinct fresh seeds, all pairs have same candidate multiset/first row, jitter cardinalities asserted, no training on previous heldout, prereg/source pinned before first-use, one full regression, first-use archive; no accepted-ref mutation.
claim_limit: Frozen synthetic local-temporal discrimination; not language generalization or reasoning.
